plan.understanding: Add a third blade matching the two existing blades, place its 0.42 mm central portion through the middle of the stack, reduce the other two central portions to 0.42 mm, and radius the new blade’s four long edges.

subtasks.goal: On source body s1, duplicate the complete existing blade identified by the 381.0 mm Z-span and faces #38,#39,#40,#42,#43,#44,#45; rotate the copy by +61.75° about the axis through [0,0,0], direction [0,1,0], so its bidirectional arms land at approximately 151.75° and 331.75° measured from +X toward +Z. Make the copied blade’s central crossing portion, corresponding to source central faces #38 and #45, 0.42 mm thick and centered in the stack at Y=6.35 mm, spanning Y=6.14..6.56 mm, while retaining the source blade’s remaining design and overall radial reach. Print the achieved arm angles and central Y limits; if the selected rotation sign instead lands an arm within about 10° of an existing blade, reverse the sign in the same attempt and confirm the final 151.75°/331.75° landing.

On body s0, reduce only the central crossing portion identified by planar faces #2 and #14 and the central full cylindrical face #15 (r=6.477 mm, axis [0,1,0], center [0,3.175,0]) from its existing 6.35 mm stack thickness to 0.42 mm; retain it as the lower layer immediately beneath the new blade, spanning Y=5.72..6.14 mm, and leave the full-thickness outer arms unchanged. Print and verify the resulting central Y limits and 0.42 mm thickness.

On body s1, reduce only the central crossing portion identified by planar face #38 and the central full cylindrical face #45 (r=6.477 mm, axis [0,1,0], center [0,9.525,0]) from its existing 6.35 mm stack thickness to 0.42 mm; retain it as the upper layer immediately above the new blade, spanning Y=6.56..6.98 mm, and leave the full-thickness outer arms unchanged. Print and verify the resulting central Y limits and 0.42 mm thickness.

Edit only the new blade body s3 (bbox [-173.821, 0.0, -101.355] to [173.821, 12.7, 101.355]) by constructing explicit swept Boolean shaving tools for its four longitudinal outer corners; do not invoke the kernel fillet/chamfer operation. Anchor the blade direction to the measured s3 longitudinal axis [0.881, 0.0, -0.473] and identify the four paths from the outer boundaries of the broad planar arm faces centered at [106.007, 12.7, -56.901], [106.007, 0.0, -56.901], [-106.007, 12.7, 56.901], and [-106.007, 0.0, 56.901]. For each path, sweep a corner-removal section whose retained boundary is an exact R1.27 mm circular arc tangent to the adjoining broad and side surfaces, then subtract that tool from s3. Limit each sweep topologically between the central shoulder transition and the short tip face so the central crossing profile and short end edges remain unchanged, as required. Do not use the four existing s3 R1.27 circular edges centered near [30.556, 6.35, -23.627], [36.568, 6.35, -12.44], [-30.556, 6.35, 23.627], and [-36.568, 6.35, 12.44] as target edges; they are local shoulder features rather than the longitudinal spans. Preserve s0, s1, and s2 unchanged. Verify with photographs from both broad sides and oblique views that all four applicable long corners are continuously rounded while the tips and center remain intact, and print measured radii of 1.27 mm from the resulting swept cylindrical/pipe surfaces.
